candidates.name: os — Miscellaneous operating system interfaces
verified_facts: Provides environment, process, descriptor, path, filesystem, and operating-system interfaces.
semantic_limits: OS calls expose state but do not by themselves prove freshness, ownership, or successful canonical publication.

candidates.name: stat — Interpreting stat results
verified_facts: Defines helpers and constants for interpreting file type and permission fields returned by stat operations.
semantic_limits: Stat metadata can race with later changes and must be sampled with path, identity, time, and digest evidence.

candidates.name: tempfile — Generate temporary files and directories
verified_facts: Provides secure temporary file and directory creation with platform-specific delete and reopen semantics.
semantic_limits: Temporary-file creation alone does not make publication atomic or durable; flush, close, replace, and readback are separate gates.

candidates.name: shutil — High-level file operations
verified_facts: Provides high-level copy, move, removal, disk usage, archive, and executable discovery helpers.
semantic_limits: High-level copy operations may not preserve every metadata field and do not prove final durability.

candidates.name: io — Core tools for working with streams
verified_facts: Defines raw, buffered, text, and in-memory stream layers with explicit encoding and newline behavior.
semantic_limits: Buffered writes are not proof of disk persistence until flush, close, and filesystem readback succeed.

candidates.name: codecs — Codec registry and base classes
verified_facts: Provides encoding and decoding interfaces, incremental codecs, stream wrappers, and error handlers.
semantic_limits: Successful decoding does not prove the source bytes are complete, authentic, or encoded as expected.

candidates.name: errno — Standard errno system symbols
verified_facts: Maps symbolic error names to operating-system error numbers for structured failure classification.
semantic_limits: An errno category does not identify root cause without the failed operation, path, process, and timing context.

candidates.name: subprocess — Subprocess management
verified_facts: Provides process creation, exit status, captured streams, and timeout handling; timeout expiration raises TimeoutExpired.
semantic_limits: A child exit code or captured output does not prove the intended executable ran unless command, image, PID, start time, and artifacts are correlated.

candidates.name: signal — Set handlers for asynchronous events
verified_facts: Provides signal constants, handlers, masks, timers, and platform-dependent process signal interfaces.
semantic_limits: Signal availability and behavior vary by platform and do not prove clean shutdown or flushed receipts.

candidates.name: time — Time access and conversions
verified_facts: Provides monotonic and performance clocks for elapsed-time measurement alongside wall-clock functions.
semantic_limits: Monotonic elapsed time cannot be directly compared across unrelated boots or hosts without additional correlation.

candidates.name: datetime — Basic date and time types
verified_facts: Provides aware and naive date-time objects, UTC offsets, arithmetic, and ISO formatting.
semantic_limits: Wall-clock timestamps can shift and require timezone, monotonic, boot, and source-order correlation.

candidates.name: threading — Thread-based parallelism
verified_facts: Provides thread identity, lifecycle, synchronization primitives, exception hooks, and live-thread enumeration.
semantic_limits: A live thread is not proof of progress; stack, owner, wait state, heartbeat, and artifact changes must agree.

candidates.name: concurrent.futures — Launching parallel tasks
verified_facts: Provides executor and future state, result retrieval, cancellation, timeout handling, and documented deadlock risks.
semantic_limits: A pending future does not prove useful work and must be bounded by ownership, timeout, and progress evidence.
